Dev Agarwal: 
Good evening and warm welcome to all of you to Deepa Jewellers Limited's First Ever Earnings 
Conference Call. We appreciate your time and participation today. 
This is an important milestone for us as a listed company and we look forward to engaging with 
the investment community and sharing our business progress, operating performance and 
growth priorities. 
To begin, I would like to provide a brief overview of our company before taking you through 
our operational and financial performance for the period under review. 
Deepa Jewellers Limited is a South India focused B2B jewellery manufacturer, with a strong 
presence in traditional vaddanam, which is a gold waist belt and CNC machine cut bangles. Our 
promoter, chairman and managing director Ashish Agarwal and our promoter and non-
executive, non-independent director Seema Agarwal embarked their journey in the gem and 
jewellery industry in the year 2001 through a partnership firm and hold an experience of 25 
years in the industry. 
I joined the company in 2021 and represent the next generation of leadership contributing 
modern business perspectives, technology-oriented thinking and contemporary strategic 
direction that support our ongoing growth. We primarily operate across Telangana, Andhra 
Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Kerala with a strong presence in the Southern Indian 
jewellery market. 
We have established long-standing relationships with leading jewellery retailers including 
Joyalukkas, Kalyan Jewellers, Lalitha Jewellers, Bhima Jewellers and other regional jewellery 
chains. 
While revenue is concentrated in Southern India, our established retail chain relationships 
enable the company to access markets beyond the region and broaden our market reach across 
India. 
We believe the shift towards organized jewellery retail chains presents a significant growth 
opportunity for organized B2B manufacturers like us. Large retail chains increasingly seek 
reliable manufacturing partners who can ensure consistent product quality, design variety and 
timely delivery and strong inventory controls as well. 
Our established capabilities and customer relationship position us well to meet these evolving 
requirements and build long-term partnerships with organized retailers. We also benefit from 
our strong presence in South India which accounts for approximately 40% of India's gem and 
jewellery market making it the largest regional market. The region's deep-rooted cultural 
affinity for gold, strong wedding and festive demand, and growing penetration of organized 
retail provide a favorable growth environment.

Over the years, we have developed a diversified portfolio spanning 16 product categories and 
approximately 110 SKUs and more than 24,000 designs. Our customer base comprises 
approximately 373 customers including 47 jewellery retail chains. Our business is primarily 
focused on jewellery manufacturing complemented by job work services which represent a 
smaller but strategically important part of our business model. 
With our expertise in traditional jewellery such as vaddanam, established customer 
relationships and expanding manufacturing capabilities, we are very well positioned to 
capitalize on these opportunities and strengthen our presence in this key market. 
With that backdrop, now I come to operational highlights for the period under review: 
One of the key developments during the period was the commencement of our in-house 
manufacturing facility in Hyderabad in September 2026. The facility, spread across 
approximately 6,700 square feet, marks an important step in strengthening our internal 
manufacturing capabilities. We believe this addition will provide us with greater operational 
flexibility, support our evolving production requirements and create a stronger foundation to 
scale our business as we continue to expand our product portfolio and customer relationships. 
Another important operational highlight is the plan to open our second sales office in Chennai 
in the 3rd Quarter end, which is the month of December. 
Another important key note which the management wishes to convey to all the investors is 
that from 1st October onwards, both the promoters and executive directors, Ashish Agarwal 
and Dev Agarwal, plan to not draw any salaries from the business. This is in respect of 
encouraging the business profitability and long-term growth in the business. So, from the 3rd 
Quarter onwards, both the promoters will not be drawing any salary from the business. 
Coming to the operational KPIs: 
During the 2nd Quarter of the Financial Year 2027, our total operating volume stood at 809 
kgs, representing a YoY increase of 13%. Processing and manufacturing volumes remained 
broadly stable at 491 kgs, while job work volumes increased to 318 kgs, registering a significant 
YoY growth of 44%. This reflects the growing contribution of job work services to our overall 
operating volume. 
For the first half of FY27, total operating volumes increased to 1327 kgs, representing YoY 
growth of 12%. Processing and manufacturing volumes stood at 783 kgs, slightly declining by 
5% YoY, while job work volumes on the other hand increased significantly by 51% YoY to 544 
kgs. Growth in job work volumes is strategically positive as the segment offers higher margins, 
lower working capital requirements and no exposure to gold price fluctuations as the gold is 
provided by the customer.

manner that complements our core manufacturing business. 
Looking ahead, we remain focused on strengthening our core manufacturing business, 
expanding our job work operations and improving the utilization of our manufacturing 
capabilities. At the same time, we recognize the importance of maintaining profitability and 
financial discipline as the business grows.

Coming to our financial performance for the first half of the financial year 2027:

Our business typically follows a seasonal pattern, with the first half contributing around 40%

into the second half along with the fresh issue proceeds is expected to support our growth 
trajectory in the second half of the financial year 2027. 
On the profitability front, EBITDA margins were impacted by lower gross margins and a 
marginal increase in employee expenses. Despite this, PAT margins improved YoY, supported 
by higher other income and a lower tax outflow.

Riddhansh Chandak: 
Hi, Dev. Congrats on the listing. Dev, since this is your maiden call, can I request you to please 
give an outlook of how clients decide on placing job work orders or a manufacturing order, the 
entire process of that. And for you specifically, when you are bidding or speaking to clients in 
regards to picking up the orders, when you are looking at pricing, is it like you have a conversion

hedging? How much is the GML? How much do you hedge on the MCX? And how does the 
entire triangulation of the hedging work internally? 
Dev Agarwal: 
Yes, answering your first question first. With every corporate client, we have two price lists and 
two agreements made. The first is with respect to the sales which we make through invoice 
basis with our own gold. And the second is sales through job work basis. And the conversion 
margin that we have in both the models is the same. There is a slight difference in the rate 
offered in terms of job work because of the lower working capital employed. For example, if 
we offer a 5% wastage to a client for sales through invoice basis, we offer about 4% of wastage 
for job work. And the 1% difference is because my working capital is not blocked. But at an 
ROCE level or an ROE level, my both the models have a similar conversion margin. 
The only difference between the margins is with respect to my working capital deployment. 
And coming to the choice of purchase between the invoice basis and the job work model, our 
clients have the flexibility to purchase in whichever model they want to because their 
purchasing pattern will depend on the availability of cash funds with them or more of old gold 
with them. So, depending upon the availability of funds or metal with them, they have a choice 
in purchasing from invoice or through job work. 
So, in all practicality, while they approach us for sales or for orders, they give us orders or they 
select goods from our inventory. And then within a day or two, they let us know their choice 
of purchasing through invoice or job work. If it is job work, they send gold to us and within 2-3 
days, we manufacture the ornaments and we supply it back to them. Whereas in case of invoice 
basis, we fix the gold rate, and we supply it to them with our own gold. So, the entire choice 
and the entire flexibility of purchasing choice is in the hands of the customer and we as a 
company are agnostic to it as both the models offer us a similar conversion margin.

Answering your second part of the question regarding hedging, as of 30th September, 94% of 
our total gold holding is hedged. We hedge through three mechanisms, the first being gold 
metal loan, the second being entering into short positions on MCX and the third model is back-
to-back price fixing or unfixed purchases from our bullion suppliers. So, with a mix of these 
three mechanisms, we continuously hedge our gold inventory. Let me explain you a bit briefly 
on how we do it. 
In case of GML, we take the physical gold from the bank on an unfixed rate basis at a nominal 
interest rate of 3.25% per annum. And we take the gold from the bank, we convert it into 
ornaments, we supply to the customer and whenever the customer fixes the gold price for it, 
we fix the same price with the bank. This helps us negate any kind of gain or loss that happens 
because of the gold price movement. 
My second hedging policy is with respect to MCX hedging. In this regard, we purchase physical 
bullion from the local market and at the same time enter into a short position on MCX futures. 
So, with the gold that we purchase, we convert it into ornaments, we supply it to the customer 
and whenever the customer fixes the price, we square off the MCX position that we had. 
The third is a policy of back-to-back pricing or unfixed purchases from bullion suppliers. In this, 
we purchase gold from our bullion suppliers on an unfixed rate basis and whenever the 
customer fixes the gold price with us, we fix the same price with our bullion supplier for the 
same quantity at the same time. So, with the mix of these three, we are able to hedge 94% of 
our gold holdings as of 30th September and as the company's policy, we aim to expand it close 
to 100% in the next two to three quarters.
